questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All Mugs are Buckets.

Some Mugs are Tumblers.

**Conclusions:**

I. All Tumblers are Mugs.

II. All Buckets are Tumblers.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5447af036cec48194bcb2058781e710cd83de95652910158e0ae279c8b65692.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All Tumblers are Mugs → Does not follow (As some Mugs are Tumblers. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. All Buckets are Tumblers → Does not follow (As all Mugs are Buckets and some Mugs are Tumblers. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion I nor II follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.

(The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)

Phycology : Algae :: Palaeontology : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic:** Field of study and its subject matter**.

Here,

Phycology : Algae → **Phycology** is the study of **Algae**.

Similarly,

Palaeontology : Fossils → **Palaeontology **is the study of Fossils.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Jasbir is an immediate neighbour of both Charan and Jagdish. Chetan is sitting second to the right of Jagdish. Palash is sitting third to the right of Charan. Pankaj is an immediate neighbour of both Charan and Chetan. Who is an immediate neighbour of both Jasbir and Palash?
questions.solution:
**Given: **Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) Chetan is sitting second to the right of Jagdish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9aa7171ffe47986944a9a98f3b079eaf20caca5aabab300b7a14cc499c83b70a.png] 

2) Pankaj is an immediate neighbour of both Charan and Chetan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1713922d516739fabefafb1c9a1ca6081fa2c825c807c6990dea03dca0d327b3.png] 

3) Jasbir is an immediate neighbour of both Charan and Jagdish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de5bf2dcde748b6dd6a3b1c02f009b3315fd1ae7c09644a2ced2d9a39bff5932.png] 

4) Palash is sitting third to the right of Charan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c92e9a05b75047db12c688f691854e310e2c6cd333a18e0771eabe07d3e12b19.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement, Jagdish is an immediate neighbour of both Jasbir and Palash.

Hence,** "Option 4"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are NOT related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(7, 245, 7),(8, 200, 5)

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: 1st number × 3rd number × 5 = 2nd number.

Now,

For, (7, 245, 7)

⇒ 7 × 7 × 5 = 245.

For, (8, 200, 5)

⇒ 8 × 5 × 5 = 200

Now checking the options:

For, (16, 560, 7)

⇒ 16 × 7 × 5 = 560.

For, (6, 270, 9)

⇒ 6 × 9 × 5 = 270.

**For, (11, 396, 9)**

**⇒ 11 × 9 × 5 = 495 ≠ 396.**

For, (12, 420, 7)

⇒ 12 × 7 × 5 = 420.

Therefore, the set (11, 396, 9) does not follow the same logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.
